instruction: A published acoustic recording has three channels: left, centre and right. Each archived take has a unique single uppercase ASCII letter as its ID. Its channel_mask records which published channels it can explain, with left worth 1, centre worth 2 and right worth 4. Combine masks by bitwise OR. A witness set must explain all three channels and be irredundant: removing any one selected take must leave at least one channel unexplained. Sort each qualifying set's IDs ascending and concatenate them without separators. Choose the lexicographically smallest resulting string under binary text ordering, with a proper prefix sorting first. Compare strings directly regardless of take count. Return exactly one row with witness_ids and take_count, the number of selected takes. At least one witness set exists. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Construct checkpoint_delta.csv with columns spool_id, resume_after, ordered by spool_id ascending in binary text order. spool_marks gives one durable checkpoint per spool. File sequence numbers are positive consecutive integers starting at 1. saved_through is the last sequence already committed, or 0 for a fresh spool. file_receipts records delivery attempts. A verified_flag of 1 proves the file is usable and 0 denotes a failed attempt. Any verified receipt suffices for that sequence, regardless of duplicate or failed attempts. Starting immediately after the saved checkpoint, advance over every consecutive usable file until the first missing or unverified sequence. resume_after is the last sequence committed after this advance. Emit only spools that advance. Receipts at or below the saved checkpoint have no effect. Inputs have no nulls and receipt row order has no significance. Submit a SQLite SELECT that writes the requested CSV report via the CSV export tool.

Prepare the revenue posting for every component of each fully delivered bundle. Each row in bundle_terms is a signed price record with a unique source_id and bundle_id, a positive total price in cents, and a short excerpt. Each component_prices row gives a component's positive standalone price in cents. Component codes are unique within a bundle. Allocate the entire signed price in proportion to standalone prices. First assign each component its whole-cent floor, then distribute the remaining cents, one per component, in descending order of the exact fractional remainder. Break remainder ties by component_code in ascending SQLite BINARY order. All supplied bundles have components, all values are non-null, and all arithmetic fits in SQLite integers. Return bundle_id, component_code, revenue_cents, source_id for every component, ordered by bundle_id and component_code ascending. Cite the signed price record used for each allocation. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Allocate up to five identical whole crates between buyers A and B. Either buyer may take any integer quantity from zero through its stated crate cap, and crates may stay at the depot. The contribution per crate is in cents after variable costs. Each buyer receiving at least one crate incurs its own fixed refrigerated delivery fee once, in cents. Maximize total contribution less delivery fees. Break ties by fewer total crates dispatched, then by fewer crates for A. There is one non-null bid per buyer, and each cap is between zero and five inclusive. Return one row with columns crates_a, crates_b, net_cents in that order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Assign one short filename to each export file, processing files by ascending file_id. The source stem and extension are supplied separately and contain only uppercase ASCII letters. Extensions are one to three letters. All names in reserved_short are occupied before allocation starts. A stem of at most eight letters gets its literal STEM.EXT if that full name is free. Otherwise, including for every stem longer than eight letters, try the first six letters of the stem followed by ~1, ~2, and so on, keeping the extension. Use the lowest free suffix and immediately occupy the full name for later files. A short stem contributes all its letters if it has fewer than six. A suffix from 1 through 9 always suffices. Return file_id and short_name in ascending file_id order. IDs are unique and have no units. Submit a SQLite SELECT that writes the requested CSV report via the CSV export tool.

A lender holds one two-period note. Its opening carrying amount equals face value minus the deferred fee. For each period, calculate effective interest on that period's opening carrying amount at the fixed periodic rate in basis points (10000 basis points equals 100%). Round interest to the nearest whole cent, with half a cent rounded up. Recognize fee income equal to rounded interest minus the cash coupon, and add that fee income to the carrying amount before starting the next period. The same coupon is paid at each period end. Report the second closing amount immediately before principal repayment. Return period_no, opening_cents, interest_cents, fee_income_cents, and closing_cents ordered by increasing period_no, one row per period. All monetary inputs and outputs are whole cents. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Allocate one 100-cent freight overage among the listed shipments. Each shipment must pay at least 20 cents. Split the available cents in proportion to capacity_used, measured in pallet positions. If any provisional shares fall below 20 cents, fix those shipments at 20 cents each and split the remaining pool proportionally among the remaining shipments. Repeat until the floor is satisfied. Round the final exact shares down to whole cents, then distribute leftover cents one per shipment in descending order of fractional remainder, breaking ties by shipment_id ascending. Return shipment_id and fee_cents ordered by shipment_id ascending. Shipment IDs are unique, capacity is positive, and the pool exceeds the sum of the minimums. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Construct invoice_footers.csv for one invoice split across export pages. The single invoice_terms row supplies a whole-invoice discount in cents. Use only charge lines whose void_flag is 0; a flag of 1 marks a cancelled line. Allocate the discount across active lines in proportion to gross_cents. Give each line the integer floor of its exact share, then distribute the leftover cents, one per line, in descending order of fractional remainder, breaking ties by ascending unique line_no across the invoice. Sum the resulting allocations by the supplied page_no. Emit only pages containing an active line. All inputs are non-null integers, line amounts are positive, and the discount is between zero and the active gross total inclusive. Output columns page_no, gross_cents, discount_cents, net_cents, sorted by page_no ascending. Net is gross less allocated discount. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Construct firing_manifest.csv with one column lot_id in ascending binary text order. Choose one or two distinct whole lots from the waiting list for a single firing. Combined shelf use must be at most 10 slots and combined mass at most 12 kilograms. The new lot_slots field gives slots for the whole lot and takes precedence. When it is null, use piece_qty times slots_each from the old layout. Null means unavailable and every lot has a usable footprint. Mass and priority points always describe the whole lot. Maximize total priority points, then minimize total slots used, then choose the lexicographically smallest sorted sequence of lot IDs (a proper prefix sorts first). IDs are distinct single uppercase letters. At least one lot fits. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

A printer must insert one plate for chapter 1 and one for chapter 2. Each pocket_offer row is an approved placement for that chapter. pocket_leaf is the numbered insertion position and opener_leaf is the chapter opening, both in leaves from the front. setup_min is handling time in whole minutes. Choose one offer per chapter such that the first pocket strictly precedes the second and their combined handling time is at most 7 minutes. Minimize the sum of absolute distances from the corresponding openers, then minimize total handling time, then choose the smaller first pocket, then the smaller second pocket. Offers are unique per chapter and pocket, and all fields are non-NULL. Return the single best layout in ordered columns first_leaf, second_leaf, drift_leaves, total_min. Return zero rows if no layout qualifies. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Every returned lot must be settled this month. For each whole lot either replace it at replace_cents or refurbish it at refurb_cents using kits_needed kits. Costs are totals in cents for the entire lot. The single shop_limit row gives available kits. The shop can open at most two refurbishment jobs, one per selected lot. Replacement uses no kits or job slots. Choose a feasible plan minimizing total settlement cost across all lots and book that cost as the provision. Break ties by fewer refurbished lots, then by the lexicographically smallest plan_code under SQLite binary ordering. A plan_code is the selected single-letter lot codes in ascending order joined by a comma, or the empty string for no refurbishment. Lot codes are unique, kit demands are positive, and no fields are null. Return one row with plan_code, kits_used, provision_cents. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Choose exactly one renewal quote for each of the EAST and WEST insurance pools. Each quote funds its own pool only. The pair's combined deposit must fit the treasury cash limit, and its combined retained exposure must fit the risk limit. Both limits are inclusive. Minimize combined annual premium, then combined deposit, then the EAST quote ID and WEST quote ID in ascending binary text order. Deposits are recoverable collateral, so exclude them from annual premium. All monetary values are integer cents. Quote IDs are unique, the limits table has one row, all fields are non-null, and a feasible pair exists. Return one row with east_quote, west_quote, east_premium_cents, west_premium_cents, total_deposit_cents, total_retained_cents. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Choose one runner for each of the opening and closing legs of a two-leg relay. Each row is an available runner-leg assignment with its projected time in whole seconds and its use of the squad's preparation budget in drill slots. An absent assignment is unavailable. The two runners must differ and their combined preparation must use at most 6 slots. Minimize total projected seconds, then minimize slots used, then choose the lexicographically smallest opening runner and then closing runner under SQLite BINARY ordering. Runner-leg pairs are unique, all fields are non-null, and a feasible pair exists. Return one row with columns opening_runner, closing_runner, total_seconds, slots_used. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Choose exactly two different reminder sessions for a survey of market stalls. Each session can run once and consumes the listed whole crew minutes. The pair has at most 10 crew minutes. Each reach row identifies a batch of outstanding questionnaires a session would recover in full. The return_count is a positive count of questionnaires, consistent wherever a batch appears. Different batches are disjoint. A batch reached twice yields its questionnaires only once. Sessions may have no reach rows. Session codes are unique, session-batch pairs are unique, and there are no NULLs. At least one pair fits. Maximize distinct questionnaires recovered, then minimize crew minutes, then choose the lexicographically smallest pair of session codes under SQLite binary order after putting the smaller code first. Output one row with first_code, second_code, recovered_count, crew_minutes. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Before the fictional Drift League closes its scorebook, fill exactly two hearing slots from the signed discrepancy notices. Each notice compares posted points with a witness tally for one bout. A NULL witness tally means the notice is incomplete and ineligible. No other field is NULL. Both slots share a budget of ten whole minutes in total, and the two notices must concern different bouts so the same discrepancy is never heard twice. A feasible pair always exists. Maximize the sum of absolute point discrepancies, then minimize total minutes, then choose the lexicographically smallest ordered pair of source IDs using SQLite binary text order. Return one row with first_ref, second_ref, points_at_issue, total_minutes, placing the smaller citation first. The figures quantify points to examine, regardless of the eventual rulings. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: For each meal where the submitted tip exceeds the reimbursable tip, report the reduction in cents and cite the governing policy notice. Each notice is primary evidence. Its structured fields encode its text. A notice takes effect at the start of effective_day and governs until the next notice for the same program. Use the service day, including when it equals the effective day. Dates are ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Each meal represents one receipt, and food_cents excludes tax and tip. Compute the maximum tip using the notice's base_kind and cap_bp (basis points, with 10000 equal to 100 percent). Round the maximum down to whole cents per receipt. All fields are non-null, amounts are nonnegative, IDs are unique within their tables, and each meal has a governing notice. Effective days are unique within each program. Return meal_id, reduction_cents, source_id in that order, sorted by meal_id ascending. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Construct the data rows of exhibit_manifest.csv, with columns in the order final_path, asset_tag. Each asset_file row is one file at its path immediately before a single round of folder moves. Each folder_move row maps one original directory to its destination. Apply the most specific matching move to the original path exactly once, preserving the slash and everything after the matched directory name. A directory matches only at a complete path-component boundary. Keep files outside all moved directories at their original paths. Paths are case-sensitive relative paths using /, with no empty or special components. All fields are non-null text, original directory names are unique, and final file paths have no collisions. There are no numeric units. Include every file, sorted by final_path in SQLite BINARY order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that writes the requested CSV report via the CSV export tool.

Construct cash_application_ack.csv for the accounts in remittance_batch. Each account has one incoming payment in whole cents. Apply it to that account's eligible open invoices in ascending due_day order, where due_day is an integer day on a shared calendar. Break equal-day ties by invoice_code in ascending binary text order. Invoice codes are unique within an account. A null hold_note means eligible and any non-null note places the invoice on hold. Each invoice can receive at most its positive open_cents, and a payment can be split across invoices. Output only invoices receiving cash. Omit any leftover unapplied payment. Use columns account_code, invoice_code, applied_cents, remaining_open_cents, where the last field is the invoice balance after this application. Sort by account_code in ascending binary text order and then by application order. All fields other than hold_note are populated. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Construct carton_corrections.csv with columns lot_id, corrected_units, source_id, ordered by lot_id ascending in binary text order. Each packing lot has a unique ID, a packing day counted in whole days from the plant's fixed epoch, a count of full cartons, and the whole-unit total currently exported. carton_bulletins contains primary packing notices for one carton model, plus their transcribed units per carton and first applicable packing day. For each lot, consider notices effective on or before its packing day. Choose the greatest effective day, breaking ties by greatest issue_seq, a unique integer publication sequence. A later-issued notice can revise a historical interval without superseding notices for later effective days. Multiply full cartons by the applicable units per carton. Emit a correction only when the exported total differs, citing the actual source_id of the controlling notice. Omit lots with no applicable notice. All fields are non-null, counts are nonnegative integers, and source IDs are unique. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Construct exhibit_corrections.csv for a translated exhibit guide. Each unique label_code is one current label. The evidence table transcribes the signed wording slips, with the source ID, primary text and its structured term, room scope, issue number and prescribed wording. All fields are present. A slip applies to its exact term_code in its named room, or in every room if room_scope is '*'. For each label prefer a room-specific slip over any general slip, then the highest integer issue_no within that scope, then the binary-smallest source_id. Apply these priorities before comparing wording. Emit only labels with an applicable slip whose prescribed text differs exactly from current_text. Include the actual winning slip ID for the copy editor. Output label_code, replacement_text, source_id ordered by label_code in binary ascending order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Construct firing_postings.csv for all kiln runs in the input. Each run has a nonnegative shared fee in whole cents. Each load line records positive whole shelf units used under an old studio key. Multiple lines may belong to one studio, and multiple old keys may map to one posting key. For each run, combine units by posting key, then apportion the fee in proportion to those combined units. First award the whole-cent floor of each exact share. Distribute the remaining cents one per posting key in descending order of fractional remainder, breaking ties by ascending posting_key in binary text order. Include participating keys even when awarded zero cents. Run keys are unique in kiln_fee, every run has usage, every load line has exactly one mapping and one run, and nothing is null. Output run_key, posting_key, fee_cents ordered by run_key then posting_key, both ascending. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Produce shift_output.csv with one row for each writer in writer_meter. The readings cover one shift. sample_no gives chronological order within a writer, with no ties. total_mib is a cumulative integer count of MiB written during the indicated run. The first non-NULL reading per writer is the opening baseline and earns no shift output. Between consecutive non-NULL readings in the same run, credit the increase. A change of run_id means the new run started from zero after the preceding valid reading, so credit its entire current reading, even if it exceeds the preceding run's reading. NULL total_mib means no measurement and is skipped. All other fields are non-NULL. Counters never decrease within a run, and every writer has a valid reading. Output writer_id, written_mib in that order, sorted by writer_id ascending. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Reconstruct the certificate history of art print P7, starting at its issue event. An issue contributes +1 active certificate. A cancellation links to the issue or re-issuance it voids. A re-issuance links to the cancellation it reverses. For either link, multiply the linked event's signed contribution by link_sign to obtain the new event's contribution. The issue has no parent and uses +1 as its seed sign. Event numbers are unique and increase along links. Follow only events descended from P7's issue. Return event_no, action, linked_event, signed_change and active_after, ordered by event_no ascending. Keep the issue's linked_event NULL. Both change and running balance are in certificates. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Construct load_manifest.csv for the single van in van_limit using the separately exported case list. Each unique case is indivisible and can travel once. The van can take one or two cases, with total mass at most capacity_kg. Two cases with the same rack_code cannot travel together because each needs exclusive use of that rack. At least one case fits. Maximize the sum of dispatch_points, then minimize total kilograms, then choose the lexicographically smallest sorted sequence of case codes under SQLite BINARY order (a shorter prefix sorts first). Codes are single uppercase ASCII letters. All inputs are non-null, kilograms are positive integers, and points are nonnegative integers. Return one row per selected case with case_code, rack_code, mass_kg, dispatch_points in that order, sorted by case_code ascending. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Construct the complete contents of handoff.csv in one result cell named csv_text. A plate qualifies only if its unique inspection slip has verdict 'pass' and its unique archive receipt exists. Either record may be absent. The receipt supplies shelf_mark. The slip supplies field_label, which may be NULL and must then serialize as an empty string. Other values are populated. Start with the literal unquoted header plate_id,field_label,shelf_mark,slip_id,receipt_id. Append one record per qualifying plate in ascending BINARY plate_id order, including the two evidence IDs. Quote every data field with double quotes, doubling every embedded double quote. Preserve all other characters verbatim. Use one LF after every record, including the header and final record. There are no numeric quantities or ties in this export. Submit a SQLite SELECT that writes the requested CSV report via the CSV export tool.

instruction: Install one indivisible exhibit in each of the library's two display cases, east and west, for the coming exhibit cycle. An exhibit may be installed at most once. Its load_kg is its mounted mass in kilograms. The inspection_note table contains signed-off primary inspection records. For each case use the record with the greatest revision_no, even when an older record allowed more weight. Its rated_kg is the structured load limit stated in its finding_text. An exhibit fits if its mass is at most that limit. Forecast visits are specific to the exhibit's placement and add across cases. Maximize combined forecast visits, breaking ties by ascending east exhibit code and then west exhibit code in binary text order. Exhibit codes, source IDs, and case/revision pairs are unique. All fields are nonnull. Return one row with columns east_exhibit, west_exhibit, forecast_visits, east_source, west_source. Cite the actual source_id of the governing inspection for each chosen placement. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Build return_bays.csv to replace two old crate-group keys with return-bay keys for one festival shift. Each group must go wholly to one bay, and each bay may receive at most one group. A route row lists an allowed group and bay pairing and the one-way carrying distance in whole metres for one crate. Each crate makes one trip. Bay capacity is in crates and must cover the entire assigned group. Among feasible complete maps minimize total crate-metres across both groups. On equal totals choose the lexicographically smallest pair of bay keys in ascending group_key order, using SQLite binary text order. There are exactly two distinct groups, unique group and bay master keys, at most one route per pair, no nulls, and at least one feasible complete map. Output group_key, bay_key, crate_metres (the contribution of that group) in ascending group_key order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Fill the two one-blank requests, slots 1 and 2. For either slot, buy a fresh blank for buy_cents or cut it free from one listed remnant. Each remnant can supply at most one slot, even if material would remain. All dimensions are millimetres. A direct fit requires both remnant dimensions to meet or exceed the corresponding blank dimensions. A quarter turn swaps the blank dimensions and is allowed only when turn_ok is 1. Each cut slip is primary evidence for the grain constraint in its row. Inputs are non-null. Minimize purchase cents, then the number of remnants consumed, then the pair of source IDs in slot order using ascending binary lexical order. Represent a purchase by the literal BUY for this comparison and in the output. Remnant IDs are unique and never BUY. Return one row with columns slip_one, source_one, slip_two, source_two, purchase_cents, citing both cut slips. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Pads L and R must observe their monuments simultaneously. Assign exactly one instrument head to each pad, using different heads. Each fit_trial row gives the signed residual in millimetres for one unique pad/head combination and the technician minutes needed to fit that head there. Missing combinations are unavailable. A NULL residual means the combination failed calibration and cannot be used. All other fields are non-NULL. One technician must complete both fittings within the single prep_window allowance, inclusive. Among feasible assignments minimize, in order, the larger absolute residual, the sum of the two absolute residuals, and total fitting minutes. Break any remaining tie by the L head ID and then the R head ID, both in binary ascending order. Return the winning row as left_head, right_head, worst_mm, combined_mm, prep_min, or no rows if infeasible. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Use SQLite to attribute each detected signal to a source interval. All times use milliseconds on the same clock. A signal may have occurred at any time from center_ms minus error_ms through center_ms plus error_ms, inclusive. Each source was active from start_ms through end_ms, inclusive. A source interval is compatible if it contains at least one possible signal time, including contact at a single endpoint. Return one row per signal with signal_id followed by interval_id. Use the interval ID only when exactly one interval is compatible. Return SQL NULL for either zero or multiple compatible intervals, even if the center time falls in one of them. Signal IDs and interval IDs are unique within their tables. Order rows by signal_id ascending using binary text order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Produce the delay-audit list for the single queue represented here. For each call, the governing bulletin is the one with the greatest effective_sec at or before queue entry. Effective seconds are unique. Omit calls predating all bulletins. The bulletin's primary text specifies the start of the audit clock, and threshold_sec gives the inclusive minimum elapsed time. Only calls with outcome 'abandoned' qualify. All times are integer seconds on the same clock. A null greeting_end_sec means there is no recorded greeting completion and excludes the call only when that timestamp is required. A null exit_sec means elapsed time cannot be established. Return call_key, elapsed_sec, source_id for qualifying calls, citing the governing bulletin's actual source_id. Order by call_key ascending. Call keys are unique. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Audit the provisional goalkeeper log, where each unique play_code represents one credited save for the listed keeper. Review notes are signed observations from the same match. Their complete finding_text uses one of three phrases. 'Shot was wide.' and 'Defender stopped the shot.' each invalidate the credit, while 'Keeper stopped the shot.' confirms it. For each logged play use the highest revision_no among final notes only. Revisions are unique within a play, and a larger revision number is newer. A play without a final note keeps its provisional credit. Return only credits to remove, one row per play, citing the actual note that controls the decision. Notes for unlogged plays are outside scope. All fields are non-null, and final_flag is 1 for final or 0 for draft. Output keeper_code, play_code, source_id, finding_text ordered by keeper_code and play_code in ascending BINARY order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Construct route_exceptions.csv with columns scan_id, observed_lane, required_lane, source_id, ordered by scan_id ascending in binary text order. A tray_scan records the lane used at scan_minute and the notice-feed position visible to the scanner, seen_pos. For that scan's diverter, consider notices received by seen_pos inclusive whose start_minute is at or before scan_minute. Choose the greatest applicable start_minute, breaking ties by greatest received_pos. Positions are unique in the notice feed. A correction to an earlier effective minute revises that entry only. Each primary notice has a unique source_id and exact notice_text in the form 'Route trays to ' followed by the entire required lane code, with no punctuation. Report only scans with an applicable notice whose required lane differs from the observed lane, citing the selected notice's actual source_id. Minutes are integer offsets from shift start, positions are unitless integers, identifiers and lane codes are case-sensitive text, and all values are non-NULL. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

For each specimen, determine whether a glaze attribution has enough independent support to enter the catalogue. Each slip records one proposed glaze. Slips with the same family_code for a specimen derive from the same underlying observation, even when their wording differs. A family casts one vote if all its slips agree and abstains if they disagree. Accept a glaze only if it receives at least two votes and strictly more votes than every rival for that specimen. Omit ties and specimens without an accepted glaze. For each family supporting an accepted glaze, cite its lexicographically smallest slip_id. Return one row per cited family with columns specimen_code, glaze_name, vote_count, slip_id, ordered by specimen_code and slip_id in ascending binary text order. vote_count counts supporting families. Slip IDs are unique and all fields are non-null. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: A workshop survey normally treats a blank return as nonresponse. Audit the narrower claim that a documented missed pickup could explain the blank. Each survey_boxes row describes one box on one route, with a planned pickup day measured in whole days from the start of the survey and a count of returned forms. Zero is a verified blank. A NULL form_count means the count is unknown. Each route_notes row is a primary operations note with a unique source ID, its short original text, a coded finding, and the inclusive first and last pickup days it covers. Return only verified blanks whose route and planned day are covered by a note. If several notes cover a box, use the one with the shortest coverage interval, breaking equal lengths by ascending source ID in SQLite binary text order. Decide whether the winning note says 'missed' only after resolving competing evidence. Output box_code, pickup_day, source_id, primary_text for each supported claim, ordered by box_code. All fields except form_count are non-NULL and box codes are unique. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Audit leaf A of the prompt book. Place entries in ascending pos, the unique physical line position within a leaf. Only cue entries consume a cue number. A non-null ink_no on a cue is a printed integer anchor. A null ink_no on a cue means the number is illegible, but the cue still occupies one place. Ignore all numbers on notes. Between each pair of consecutive cue anchors on A, compare the increase in printed number with the number of cue entries after the first anchor through and including the second. Report only disagreements. A positive excess means the numbering advanced farther than the surviving cue entries explain. Do not extrapolate beyond the anchors. Return start_pos, end_pos, cue_steps, excess in ascending start_pos order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Construct placeholder_repairs.csv from two offline token inventories for one source file and its proposed translation. A row records one occurrence of a named placeholder in the indicated message. Identical rows represent separate occurrences. All cells are present. The inventories are complete, so a missing message and token combination has count zero on that side. Token order may change freely. Compare exact token names within each message across the union of both inventories. Emit one row for every count mismatch with columns message_code, token_name, count_delta. instruction: Each numbered sampling period counts amber readings, blue readings, and scheduled observations whose color is missing. Each missing observation could be either color. Apply this rule symmetrically. A tie or an indeterminate majority breaks a run, as does a gap in period numbers. Locate the earliest run of at least two consecutive periods with the same confirmed majority. Report only its first two periods, even if it continues. Return at most one row with start_period, confirmed_period (the second period), and majority_color ('amber' or 'blue'), in that order. Periods are integer indices with one row per recorded period. Return no rows if no run qualifies. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

For the observation window from second 100 inclusive to second 160 exclusive, report each queue's maximum number of simultaneously waiting calls and the earliest integer second at which it reached that maximum. Each unique wait_key represents one call. A call waits from enter_sec inclusive to leave_sec exclusive. A null leave_sec means the call was still waiting at the end of observation. A zero-duration wait occupies no time. Include calls already waiting when observation began. Report only queues with at least one occupied second in the window. Return queue_code, peak_calls, first_peak_sec, ordered by queue_code ascending. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Construct press_pick.csv with one row for the entire run. Select exactly one cover file and one insert file from the candidate versions. Both must have the same finished width in millimeters, and their combined whole-run sheet requirement must fit the 100 sheets on hand. Quality points are integer scores on a common scale. Maximize the lower of the two component scores because either component can limit the booklet's grade. Break ties by higher combined score, then fewer sheets used, then ascending cover_id and insert_id using SQLite's binary text order. File IDs are unique within each table, no values are null, and a feasible pair exists. Return cover_id, insert_id, grade_points (the lower score), sheets_used, in that order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Construct catalog_manifest.csv for a catalog uploader. Choose one of the offered rows_per_file settings for the whole run. In ascending seq_no order, place exactly that many consecutive catalog rows in each file except the last, which takes the remainder. Sequence numbers are unique and contiguous from 1. Each file adds a 2-byte header; row_bytes already includes the encoded row and its line ending. Every individual file must fit within 13 bytes including its header. Among feasible settings minimize the number of files, then choose the smaller rows_per_file. At least one setting is feasible. All inputs are positive integers without nulls, and offered settings are distinct. Emit one row per chosen file with columns rows_per_file, file_no, first_seq, last_seq, file_bytes. Number files from 1 and sort by file_no ascending. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

The fictional Chalk Quay Weekly has six lines and at most two type frames left in its correction strip. Each docket row is a verified correction supported by the cited primary note. One correction consumes one frame and its full positive line count. Corrections in the same bundle reach exactly the same copies, so the editor permits at most one per bundle. Different bundles have disjoint circulation. Choose a nonempty feasible set maximizing total affected copies reached. Break ties by fewer total lines, then by the lexicographically smallest ascending sequence of docket IDs, with a proper prefix first. IDs are unique single uppercase ASCII letters within the docket. Every docket row has exactly one matching note, all values are nonnull, and at least one correction fits. Return one row per chosen correction with columns docket_id, copies_reached, source_id, sorted by docket_id ascending. Copies are whole newspaper copies. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: A listening-station display has two citation slots and a budget of 100 printed characters across the two excerpts. Choose exactly two distinct slips about the station's recording. instruction: Audit adjacent sightings in each object's documented itinerary. Integer visit_no gives the established visit order within the object, with gaps allowed. Each cited note places the object at a gallery on one unknown integer day between early_day and late_day inclusive, measured from the same catalogue epoch. For each adjacent pair in visit order, consult the minimum elapsed days for its directed route. Report a conflict only if even the most favorable choice of days for that pair falls short. Scope is pairwise feasibility only. Skip same-gallery pairs and routes without a recorded minimum. Return object_code, from_note, to_note, shortfall_days, ordered by object_code in binary order then by the destination visit_no ascending. shortfall_days is the positive difference between the required minimum and the maximum possible elapsed days. instruction: Calculate interest payable for each deposit account for days 1 through 4 inclusive. opening_cents is the balance immediately before day 1. Each movement is a separate signed posting in cents that takes effect before that day's close. Include all postings on an in-scope day, including multiple postings on the same day. Ignore postings outside the period. A day without postings carries forward the preceding balance. All closing balances are nonnegative. Interest accrues at 3 basis points per day on each closing balance, without compounding. Round the four-day interest total once to the nearest cent, with exact half cents rounded upward. Account codes are unique in deposit_openings, and no fields are null. Return account_code, balance_day_cents (the sum of the four closing balances), and interest_cents, ordered by account_code ascending. Include accounts without movements. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Produce frozen_locations.csv representing the archive catalog at the end of minute 30. Each catalog_event is a complete update for one segment. A non-NULL shelf_code places the segment on that shelf, replacing any earlier placement. A NULL shelf_code withdraws the segment until a subsequent placement. Apply only events with minute_no at or before 30, in increasing minute_no order, breaking same-minute ties by increasing event_no. event_no is globally unique and need not increase across different minutes. All fields except shelf_code are non-NULL. Segments start absent. Include only segments present at freeze, with columns segment_id, shelf_code, placement_event (the event_no of the controlling placement). Sort by shelf_code ascending, then segment_id ascending, using binary text order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that writes the requested CSV report via the CSV export tool.

Close the 2026-04 subscription royalty waterfall. Each row in guarantee_terms represents one catalog covered that month. Its earned_cents are ordinary royalties already funded outside the reserve. The floor is a guarantee on total royalties for that catalog. Use the single April reserve to cover shortfalls, processing lower pay_rank first and breaking rank ties by catalog_id in ascending binary text order. A catalog can receive a partial top-up. Ordinary royalties above one catalog's floor belong to that catalog. Report every covered catalog, including those receiving zero reserve funds. All inputs are non-null, amounts are nonnegative integer cents, catalog IDs are unique, and monthly_reserves has one row per listed month. Return catalog_id, topup_cents, payable_cents, unmet_cents in processing order. Payable includes ordinary royalties and the funded top-up. Unmet is the portion of the floor still unfunded. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Choose one indivisible pickup slot for a gallery crate. Both packing and hoist setup must be complete by the slot start, with equality allowed. Each evidence row is a primary crew note. Its ready_hour is the completion time stated in note_text, in whole hours from project start. For each of the two operations use the note with the greatest revision, even when a correction moves completion earlier. Revisions are unique within each operation. Slots list their start and arrival hours from the same origin and their total fee in cents. Arrival after hour 18 is unacceptable. Among feasible slots minimize fee, then arrival hour, then slot_id in ascending binary text order. At least one slot qualifies. All fields are non-null, and slot and source IDs are unique within their tables. Return one row with columns slot_id, fee_cents, packing_source, hoist_source. Cite the actual controlling source ID for each operation. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Finance measures gross retention of opening monthly recurring revenue by contract portfolio. Each row is one component of a contract's monthly run rate in integer cents at the opening and closing snapshots. NULL means the component was absent at that snapshot and contributes zero. Amounts are nonnegative, identifiers are non-NULL, and each contract belongs to one portfolio. Sum components within each contract at each snapshot. A contract with positive opening revenue contributes its opening total to the baseline and the smaller of its opening and closing totals to retained revenue. Thus a component replacement can preserve contract value, while expansion of one contract cannot cover another contract's loss. Exclude contracts with zero opening revenue and portfolios without a positive baseline. Return portfolio, opening_cents, retained_cents, lost_cents, sorted by portfolio ascending. Lost revenue is opening revenue less retained revenue. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Choose one departure option for the outbound bus. All times are integer minutes after 08:00. Each feeder group needs walk_min minutes after arrival to reach the outbound bay. It connects if it is ready by departure and its wait from readiness through departure is at most max_wait_min, with both endpoints inclusive. A NULL arrival means the feeder is cancelled. Every connecting group boards in full, so reject options where connecting riders exceed the seats left after through riders. Maximize connecting riders, then minimize total rider-minutes waited by those who connect, then choose the earlier departure. Departure minutes are unique. Return the single winning row with columns depart_min, riders, rider_wait_min, source_id. Cite the seat notice attached to the winning option. The numeric seat limit transcribes its notice. All other fields are non-NULL. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Close each plant's single production period. Each plant_period row covers one plant making one homogeneous product, with no opening stock or work in process. normal_units is positive normal capacity, made_units is actual good output, and unsold_units is the portion still held. direct_unit_cents is inventoriable direct cost per good unit. Allocate the plant's fixed_pool_cents equally per unit using the greater of normal capacity and actual output as the denominator. The fixtures give whole-cent rates. Expense any pool amount unallocated to production, including the entire pool during shutdown. Report closing finished goods cost and the period's idle capacity expense in cents. All fields are non-null, plant codes are unique, and there are no tie choices. Return plant_code, closing_goods_cents, idle_expense_cents ordered by ascending plant_code. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Audit every unordered pair of field slips for the same mark measured against the same datum. A slip gives a height estimate in millimetres and its own symmetric tolerance in millimetres. Treat both endpoints of each permitted height interval as included. Report a pair only if the intervals are disjoint. Give the positive distance between their nearest endpoints as gap_mm. Different datums have unrelated zeros. A NULL tolerance means the interval is unknown, so omit pairs involving that slip. Tolerances otherwise are nonnegative, source IDs are unique, and all remaining fields are non-NULL. Return mark_id, first_source, second_source, gap_mm with the smaller source ID first under BINARY ordering. Sort by descending gap_mm, then ascending mark_id, first_source, second_source. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Choose one or two distinct preloaded racks for a single outbound truck run. Each row in rack_offer is one indivisible rack for a different station. Its slot_use is the number of truck floor slots it occupies, and saved_trips is the forecast number of otherwise missed rider trips it would restore. These benefits add across destinations. The single truck_card row documents the active loading rule and gives the available floor slots. Maximize total saved trips within the slot limit, then minimize slots used, then choose the lexicographically smallest ordered pair of rack IDs using SQLite BINARY order, with NULL sorting first. Put the smaller ID first for a two-rack load. At least one rack fits. Inputs contain no nulls. Return one row with columns first_rack, second_rack, used_slots, saved_trips, source_id, in that order. instruction: Choose one approved possession window for a mandatory inspection on one station throat. A window blocks every listed movement on that throat with a positive-duration overlap. All intervals are half-open in integer minutes after midnight. Each movement belongs to one service booking. Displacing any movement cancels its entire booking and incurs the booking's compensation once in cents. A NULL compensation denotes a protected booking whose movements must all remain available. A window touching any protected movement for positive duration is infeasible. Minimize total compensation, then the number of canceled bookings, then start minute, then binary ascending permit ID. An empty window of traffic costs zero. All intervals have positive length, every movement references an existing booking, booking and permit IDs are unique within their tables, and only compensation can be null. At least one window is feasible. Return one row with ordered columns permit_id, canceled_qty, compensation_cents. The permit ID must cite the selected possession permit. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Choose one of three designs A, B, and C by instant runoff. Each row is an anonymous group of ballot_count identical ballots ranking all three designs, once each, from first to third. Count each ballot for its highest-ranked remaining design. A design wins immediately with strictly more than half of all ballots. Otherwise eliminate exactly one remaining design with the fewest votes, including designs with zero votes. Break elimination ties by eliminating C before B before A. Transfer the eliminated design's ballots and repeat, applying the same rule even if the final two designs tie. Return exactly one row with winner (design code), winning_round (integer, starting at 1), and winning_votes (number of ballots credited to the winner in that round), in that order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Use SQLite to calculate the integral of sheet area over one drying pass, from the first sample through the last. Each sample gives elapsed time in seconds and the sheet's width and length in centimetres. Between consecutive samples, width and length each change linearly with time. The instantaneous area is their product. Return one row with one column, area_cm2_s, in square-centimetre seconds. Sample times are distinct and there are at least two samples. The exact total for each supplied dataset is an integer. Preserve fractional contributions until the total is formed. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Prepare the consolidation adjustment for each material in closing_blend. A depot commingles all intake for a material and uses periodic weighted-average cost. There is no opening stock. Each intake row gives positive units received, the depot's book price per unit in cents, and the group's historical cost per unit in cents. For external purchases the two prices coincide. Internal transfers can have positive or negative margins, and both must be reversed on the share still held. Each unique closing material has intake, and held_units is its unsold quantity. Compute closing inventory on the group's basis and the signed reduction from depot closing value to group closing value. Weight by received units before multiplying by the closing quantity. Both closing valuations are exact whole cents in these fixtures. All fields are non-null. Receipt sequence and ties have no bearing. Return material, group_value_cents, elimination_cents in ascending material order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Price a date change for one passenger flying the two coupons of ticket T together. Each offer is a complete replacement itinerary covering both coupons. Its through fare is the price for the entire trip in cents. Both carriers' change rules must permit the change. For an eligible offer, the passenger pays the positive increase over the original through fare, or zero if the fare fell, plus the larger of the two carriers' change fees. Charge that fee once per ticket. Choose the offer with the lowest amount due, breaking ties by offer_id in ascending binary text order. Return one row with offer_id, fare_increase_cents, change_fee_cents, and due_cents in that order. Each offer has exactly one rule for each of its two carriers, and at least one offer is eligible. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Calculate each operating day's imbalance invoice. Each reading gives a signed deviation in whole kWh and an integer minute from midnight (0 through 1439). Positive means surplus and negative means shortfall. The permitted netting intervals start at midnight and last 15 minutes each. Minute 15 begins the second interval. Sum all deviations in the same day and interval, including readings tied on minute. Charge 2 cents per net surplus kWh and 5 cents per net shortfall kWh. An empty or balanced interval costs zero. Add the interval charges for each day with readings. Return day_no and penalty_cents in that order, one row per day sorted by ascending day_no. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Calculate the acquisition-date fair value and signed carrying-value adjustment for each acquired inventory lot. Quantities are units. All monetary inputs are integer cents per unit. For RAW lots, use the replacement cost in the applicable supplier quote. For FIN and WIP lots, start with the quoted selling price of one finished unit, deduct selling costs and the profit allowance for selling effort, and also deduct the lot's remaining completion cost and profit allowance for completion effort. FIN lots have zero remaining completion amounts. Multiply by quantity before subtracting the lot's total carrying value. For each lot use the newest quote for its item and required quote kind (REPLACE for RAW, SELL otherwise) dated on or before the common valuation date of 2026-03-31. Dates are ISO calendar dates. For same-day ties choose the lexicographically smallest source_id under binary ordering. Each lot has an eligible quote. The evidence text is the supplier's or buyer's original price statement, and unit_cents is its numeric transcription. Cite the selected statement by its actual source_id. A null selling cost or selling profit allowance means zero. There are no other nulls. Output lot_id, source_id, fair_value_cents, adjustment_cents in ascending binary lot_id order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: A main has exactly two independent feed paths, east and west. Close exactly one candidate valve on each path to isolate the main. Closing a valve interrupts every service block listed for it in valve_effect. A block affected by both closures experiences one outage. Minimize the number of distinct service connections interrupted, then minimize the sum of the two valves’ turn_minutes (minutes of operator work), then prefer the alphabetically first east valve code followed by the alphabetically first west valve code under SQLite BINARY ordering. Return one row with columns east_valve, west_valve, connections_out, work_minutes. Valve codes and block codes are unique in their respective catalogs. Effect pairs are unique and reference those catalogs. A valve with no effect rows interrupts zero service connections. All values are non-null. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Calculate the indirect-method operating cash flow adjustment attributable to each depot ledger balance during the reporting period. Return one row per balance with columns balance_id, trading_change_cents, operating_adjustment_cents, ordered by balance_id ascending. Opening and closing balances are positive carrying amounts in cents, including for liabilities. Each movement is signed in the carrying amount's own direction. The closing balance already includes every listed movement. Remove acquisition-date and currency-translation movements, identified by move_kind 'acquired' and 'translation', from the closing-minus-opening change. A 'trade' movement documents ordinary activity already in that change and stays in it. An increase in a trading asset consumes cash and an increase in a trading liability provides cash. An absent movement contributes zero. Balance IDs are unique in depot_balance, all movements belong to a listed balance, repeated movement amounts are separate postings, and no values are null. Include zero adjustments. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Two scans each show a physical impression of page 7. Find the caption on the impression named in job. The caption occupies the half-open interval [4,12), measured in characters from offset zero along the caption line of the unsplit page. Join one left-scan fragment starting at 4 to one right-scan fragment ending at 12. The fragments must meet at exactly the same offset and both must come from the requested impression. Each fragment contains one character per offset, including spaces, and its stored text is in reading order. Return the distinct reconstructed strings in a single column named caption, sorted in binary text order. Identical reconstructions count once. The supplied fragments yield one physical caption. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

At each hourly kiln departure, choose a load from the batches offered for that departure only. Each whole batch occupies one position on a two-position cart. Total mass may be at most 10 kg, inclusive. Batch codes are unique within a departure, masses and avoided delay costs are positive integers, and no input is null. Maximize the sum of avoided delay costs in cents. Break ties by lower total mass, then fewer batches, then the lexicographically smallest sequence of selected batch codes sorted in binary order. An empty load is feasible. Return one row per represented departure ordered by departure_no, with columns departure_no, first_batch, second_batch, load_kg, saved_cents. Use null for each unused position and zero totals for an empty load. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

For each kiln represented in probe_pairs, report covered_minutes and discordant_minutes during minutes [0,20) of one firing. Each row simultaneously updates both probe readings in whole degrees Celsius. Its state applies from tick_min up to the next update for that kiln, or minute 20 if there is none. An update before minute 0 can establish the opening state. Time before the first update is uncovered. A null reading explicitly makes the pair unavailable until the next update. Count a minute as covered only when both readings are available, and as discordant only when covered and the absolute difference is at least 5 degrees. Each kiln has at most one update per tick. Return columns kiln_code, covered_minutes, discordant_minutes in ascending kiln_code order, including kilns with zero coverage. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

For each kiln, estimate its mean electrical load over the usable portions of its meter history. tick_min is elapsed time in minutes and meter_wh is a cumulative watt-hour reading. A NULL reading means the visit produced no measurement. Within each kiln, discard those visits, sort the remaining reads by time, and consider each consecutive pair. A pair is usable if its elapsed time is at most 90 minutes and its meter change is nonnegative. A decrease indicates a reset during that pair. The lower reading can still start the next pair. Pool the energy and duration of all usable pairs before converting to watts, then round down to an integer. Include zero-change pairs in the duration. Return only kilns with usable time. The ordered output columns are kiln_code, covered_min, mean_watts. Sort by kiln_code ascending. Times are unique within a kiln and all fields except meter_wh are non-NULL. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Choose exactly one cycle for kiln E and one for kiln W for the next recovery shift. Each candidate gives the additional saleable tiles recovered, whole technician minutes used, and whole grams of glaze consumed. Benefits and resource use add across kilns. The single shift_limits row sets inclusive shared caps on both resources. Maximize total recovered tiles among feasible pairs. Break ties by fewer total technician minutes, then fewer total glaze grams, then ascending east cycle_code and west cycle_code using binary text order. Cycle codes are unique within each kiln, all values are non-NULL, and at least one feasible pair exists. Return one row with east_cycle, west_cycle, recovered_tiles, tech_min, glaze_g. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Choose one plan for each of two product lines, cups and tiles, for a single shift. Each menu row is a complete indivisible option for that line, including its idle option. Plan codes are unique within a line. All produced pieces sell. Contribution in cents equals pieces times selling price less variable cost per piece, minus the full one-time setup cost shown for that option. Apply both shared shift limits from the single signed shift brief. Maximize combined contribution. Break ties by fewer total kiln minutes, then ascending binary cup plan code, then ascending binary tile plan code. Return exactly one row with cup_plan, tile_plan, kiln_minutes, clay_kg, contribution_cents, source_id in that order. All fields are nonnull integers or text as declared. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: Compare kiln methods A and B on accepted tiles per operating hour. Each method has one row for each of two tile sizes, with positive operating hours. Within each size, compare accepted tiles divided by hours. For the pooled comparison, weight each size's rate by that method's own operating hours, equivalently dividing total accepted tiles by total hours for each method. Set reversal to 1 only when the same method has a strictly higher rate in both sizes and a strictly lower pooled rate. Any tie or mixed within-size ordering gives 0. Decide reversal using unrounded rates. Return one row with columns a_tiles_per_hour, b_tiles_per_hour, reversal, showing the two pooled rates rounded to three decimal places. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Calculate the cost of building one kit, including its nested assemblies. Within each parent, each distinct slot is required. Rows for the same parent and slot are substitutes. Select the row with the lowest priority number, breaking ties by child code in ascending binary text order. Multiply quantities along each selected path. A purchased part used in two required slots contributes its cost in both slots. Assemblies have no direct cost, all leaves have a purchase price, and the bill is acyclic. Return one row with root_part followed by cost_cents in whole cents. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Estimate the probability that a lamp survives beyond day 2 using the Kaplan–Meier estimator. Each lamp starts working at day 0 and has one exit record. An exit marked failed is an observed failure. An exit marked censored means observation ended while the lamp still worked. Start survival at 1. At each distinct failure day up to and including day 2, multiply survival by (number at risk minus failures that day) divided by number at risk. Count all lamps with exit_day at least that day as at risk, including lamps censored on the same day. Apply tied failures together. A day with only censoring contributes no factor. Return one row with the single column survival_day_2, a probability from 0 to 1 rounded to six decimal places after multiplication. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Reconstruct the shelf of each listed holding at the end of its own inventory close day. Day numbers are integers on one shared calendar and include the entire day. A shelf note records either a completed physical sighting or a planned move. Only a sighting on or before the holding's close day establishes its location. Among eligible sightings use the latest day, breaking a same-day tie by the larger slip number, which denotes the later entry. Slip numbers are unique source IDs. The shelf code is the indexed location in the slip text. Omit holdings without an eligible sighting. All input fields are non-null. Return holding_code, shelf_code, slip_no in ascending holding_code order. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

instruction: For the single funding request, buy exactly need_units whole foreign currency units using one ticket from each of desks A and B. Each ticket can be used once. A zero-unit ticket represents skipping that desk. A ticket that delivers after cutoff_day is ineligible. The sum of hold_cents for the two tickets must fit the request’s USD collateral limit, cap_cents. Collateral is returned and is separate from purchase cost. Minimize the sum of the two all-in USD prices in price_cents. Break cost ties by ascending A ticket_code, then ascending B ticket_code, using SQLite binary text order. Ticket codes are unique and at least one pair qualifies. Days are integer day numbers on the same calendar. All fields are non-null. Return one row with a_code, b_code, cost_cents, hold_cents for the selected pair. Submit a SQLite SELECT that produces the requested output using the supplied tables.

Choose a booking for one panel batch that requires sanding followed by waxing. Each row is a supplier certificate that also quotes the work. The structured fees and durations transcribe its primary text. A NULL stage fee and duration mean that stage is unavailable. Assign one certificate to each stage. Construct quantity_patch.csv for rows where the importer stored the wrong individual-piece count. For each seed tray, quantify the chance that two seeds drawn uniformly without replacement belong to different species. Each row gives the seed count for one identified species in one packet. instruction: Construct credit_adjustments.csv at the close of a catalog cleanup. Each contract prepays a single fee in integer cents for a positive number of equal catalog slots. instruction: Recover the original signed net-unit count on each receipt in one scanner batch. Positive units are purchases and negative units are returns. Receipts are numbered consecutively from 1.
